articles.title: AI Boom Risks a ‘Corporate Extinction Event’: Paul
articles.summary: Sherry Paul, managing director and private wealth advisor at Morgan Stanley, says companies that fail to embrace AI risk being overtaken by competitors that use the technology to boost productivity and profitability. “We move into what I call the corporate extinction event,” Paul says on “Bloomberg Surveillance,” comparing the disruption to Netflix overtaking Blockbuster. This interview aired Sept. 17, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 💻 A Full-Fledged Trading Engine for the Node.js Ecosystem
articles.summary: You can check out the project repo here Over the past five years the Node.js ecosystem has stabilized. Nothing fundamentally new shows up in it: we discuss why Fastify beats Express, choose between Prisma and Drizzle, argue about ESM versus CommonJS, and swap one bundler for another that does the same thing, only faster. The niches are taken, the tools are mature, the hype has moved to neighboring runtimes. That is good news for production and boring news for an engineer. Which makes it all the more interesting when an entire new application domain opens up in the ecosystem. Backtest as one of the execution modes The library is a toolkit for algorithmic trading that extends Node.js into territory historically ruled by Python alone: Backtrader, VectorBT, Freqtrade. The very same trading strategy runs in both live and backtest without changes backtest-kit dashboard The difference is fundamental. articles.title: Status Of Anthropic IPO As AI Fears Mount
articles.summary: Bloomberg's Anthony Hughes joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Anthropic is preparing for its IPO and has picked Nasdaq as its listing venue. The Claude chatbot maker is seeking to raise as much as or more than SpaceX in an IPO that could take place as soon as October, Bloomberg has reported. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Meta CEO Weighs In on AI Safety Debate

articles.title: CetinLM: Breaking the Billion-Dollar AI Infrastructure Myth
articles.summary: As software engineers, we have been conditioned to accept a deeply flawed premise: that entering the Artificial Intelligence research space requires multi-billion-dollar infrastructure, massive enterprise GPU clusters, and infinite venture capital. The mainstream tech narrative has turned language model pre-training into a game of brute-force computational scale. But scale alone is not engineering. Recently, an independent research line under the architecture CetinLM proved that localized precision engineering can completely dismantle this high-capex barrier to entry. Built entirely from scratch under the corporate umbrella of Me Force Technology, the project successfully navigated past the 2.05 Billion training tokens milestone. The entire operation—from raw data engineering to the final optimization steps—is running natively inside a standard home desktop environment on a single, standalone 16GB NVIDIA RTX consumer GPU.
